children: Shares of Snap Inc. (SNAP) climbed nearly 1% in overnight trading late Wednesday amid growing investor interest in the social media company. SNAP stock has fallen over 30% so far this year, with retail traders speculating about a potential buyout.
Meanwhile, company insiders, including CFO Douglas Hott, Chief Commercial Officer Harris Ronan, and Chief Accounting Officer Rebecca Morrow, sold SNAP shares worth nearly $2.1 million.

According to regulatory filings with the Securities and Exchange Commission, Hott sold 129,203 shares on Nov. 16, at a weighted average price of $5.0898 per share, for approximately $657,617. The sale was made to cover tax withholding obligations associated with the settlement of restricted stock units (RSUs).

Ronan sold 140,437 shares on Nov. 16, at a weighted average price of $5.0896 per share, for approximately $714,768. He sold another 100,000 shares on Nov. 17 at a weighted average price of $5.4219 per share, worth approximately $542,190. Both transactions of 240,437 shares, worth about $1.26 million, were under a pre-arranged Rule 10b5-1 trading plan.

Morrow sold 19,221 shares on Nov. 16 at a weighted average price of $5.0918, worth a total of about $97,869. She sold another 15,520 shares on Nov. 18 at an average price of $5.5215, worth approximately $85,694. Both transactions were under a pre-arranged Rule 10b5-1 trading plan and totalled approximately $183,563.
